messages.author: d0d836433f1157c5
messages.subject: Blavaan models' comparison
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am new to these macro but I used to work with lavaan. I need to compare different models by using Bayesian sem. I am not pretty sure about what function is better to be implemented. If I have 8 different models, starting with the first two comparison, should I use bcfa or bsem (all have latent variables)? 
These two are my models:
Model 1

Model1 <- 'INTENTION =~ INTENT1_T1 + INTENT2_T1 + INTENT3_T1
ATTAFF =~ ATTAFF1_T1 + ATTAFF2_T1 + ATTAFF3_T1 + ATTAFF4_T1
ATTCOGN =~ ATTSTR1_T1 + ATTSTR2_T1 + ATTSTR3_T1 + ATTSTR4_T1
SOCNORM =~ SUBJN1_T1 + SUBJN2_T1 + SUBJN3_T1 
SELFEFFICACY =~ EFF1_T1 + EFF2_T1 + EFF3_T1+ EFF4_T1 + EFF5_T1 + EFF6_T1
+ EFF7_T1 + EFF8_T1 + EFF9_T1 + EFF10_T1 + EFF11_T1 + EFF12_T1

INTENTION ~ ATTAFF + ATTCOGN + SOCNORM + SELFEFFICACY'

Model 2
<- 'INTENTION =~ INTENT1_T1 + INTENT2_T1 + INTENT3_T1
ATTAFF =~ ATTAFF1_T1 + ATTAFF2_T1 + ATTAFF3_T1 + ATTAFF4_T1
ATTCOGN =~ ATTSTR1_T1 + ATTSTR2_T1 + ATTSTR3_T1 + ATTSTR4_T1
SOCNORM =~ SUBJN1_T1 + SUBJN2_T1 + SUBJN3_T1 
SELFEFFICACY =~ EFF1_T1 + EFF2_T1 + EFF3_T1+ EFF4_T1 + EFF5_T1 + EFF6_T1
+ EFF7_T1 + EFF8_T1 + EFF9_T1 + EFF10_T1 + EFF11_T1 + EFF12_T1

INTENTION ~ ATTAFF + ATTCOGN + SOCNORM + SELFEFFICACY + PASTWEEK'

I run this syntax:

fit1b <- bcfa <- bcfa(Model1, data=BSEM, group = 'pro_pre')
summary(fit1b, fit.measures=TRUE, ci = TRUE, rsquare=TRUE)


fit2b <- bcfa(Model2, data=BSEM, group = 'pro_pre')
summary(fit2b, fit.measures=TRUE, ci = TRUE, rsquare=TRUE)

blavCompare(fit2b, fit1b)


The output is wired: First of all, degrees of freedom are NA, as well as Test statistic for each group and AIC (but I have BIC). Second, I can only see the Estimate value for each latent variable but none index else. 
I read in this blog that the multigroup analyses are not available for blavaan, but despite the multigroup analyses I really need to compare my models, please can you tell me how should I do?
Thank you very much in advance!!!!

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Blavaan models' comparison
parts:
Giulia,

A few initial responses here:

- I believe that you would want to use bsem instead of bcfa, because you have regressions between latent variables. But I'm also not sure that it will make a difference here.

- You can do multigroup analyses in blavaan. The multi*level* analyses are not yet available.

- I agree that the output sounds weird. There must be some problem. Are you able to send me the data, off-list if needed?

Best,
Ed

messages.subject: Re: Blavaan models' comparison
parts:
Hello Giulia,

The main problem is that you are overwriting the function "bcfa" in these lines:

fit1b <- bcfa <- bcfa(Model1, data=BSEM, group = 'pro_pre')
summary(fit1b, fit.measures=TRUE, ci = TRUE, rsquare=TRUE)

Just change it to this:

fit1b <- bcfa(Model1, data=BSEM, group = 'pro_pre')
summary(fit1b, fit.measures=TRUE, ci = TRUE, rsquare=TRUE)

This should solve your problem. 

Thanks.

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Blavaan models' comparison
parts:
Esteban,

Thanks, I missed that part of the code. We also discovered off-list that, if you load lavaan after blavaan, then R will use the lavaan summary() method instead of the blavaan summary() method on a blavaan object. Then the results look odd. So I think it is best to only do

library(blavaan)

which will also load lavaan as a by-product.

Best,
Ed

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Blavaan models' comparison
parts: - I believe that you would want to use bsem instead of bcfa, because you have regressions between latent variables. But I'm also not sure that it will make a difference here.

cfa() and sem() are clones in lavaan; identical wrappers around lavaan() that simply set the same defaults:

int.ov.free = TRUE, int.lv.free = FALSE,
auto.fix.first = TRUE, auto.fix.single = TRUE, auto.var = TRUE,
auto.cov.lv.x = TRUE, auto.cov.y = TRUE, auto.th = TRUE,
auto.delta = TRUE, auto.efa = TRUE

I expect the same holds for bcfa() and bsem(), unless you designed the wrappers to differ. 

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
